column1: # Printed cumulative values that a LATER report withdraws without saying so.
# What an entry asserts. On this report the source printed a cumulative for
# these places that the following reports do not build on: they continue
# from the value before it, adding their own day's counts, as though this
# report's value had never been printed. The entry is a reading of the
# reports' arithmetic, quoted below, and it names the report whose numbers
# show the withdrawal.
# What it does. `build_streams.py` treats the named quantity as unobserved for
# the named places on this report date, in every route that reads it (the
# zone table, the provincial summary, the prose, the front-page tile). The
# daily row for that date is then absent rather than a clamped zero, so the
# next report's row covers both days, and `n_report_days` says it absorbed
# one. The weekly streams forward-fill across the date as they do for any
# report that does not print the quantity. Nothing is guessed: the withdrawn
# value is not replaced by any number, it is simply not used.
# Why not the other registers. `retrospective_batches.tsv` says a movement
# holds records belonging to earlier days; here the movement was reversed by
# the next report, so the records are not back-dated, they are withdrawn.
# `rejected_routes.tsv` says a route misread a document; here every route
# reads the page correctly and the page itself is what the source took back.
# `window_merged_rows.tsv` deletes a clamped-zero row after differencing;
# here the value is removed before differencing, so no deficit opens at all.
# Each entry is checked against the build: the SHA-256 prefix must match the
# held PDF (a revised document returns for a fresh judgement), and the entry
# must remove at least one printed value (an entry that removes nothing is
# stale and stops the build).
# COLUMNS
#   sitrep        report number whose value is withdrawn
#   date          its data date
#   sha256_16     first 16 hex characters of that PDF's SHA-256
#   quantity      the extraction's value column (cum_cases or cum_deaths)
#   places        comma-separated stream slugs; a province slug covers its
#                 zone, unassigned and province rows, `national` the national
#                 rows and the front-page tile
#   withdrawn_by  the report(s) whose numbers continue from the earlier base
#   verified_by   who decided, and when
#   note          the arithmetic and the source's words
sitrep

column8: Sitrep 169 (faits saillants): "le nombre total de décès passe de 3436 à 3750 ce qui ramène le total général des décès à 5 372"; its Tableau 1 prints Ituri 3 769 and national 5 372. Sitrep 170 prints Ituri 3 483 and national 5 103 with no explanation: 168's 3 436 + 19 (169's day) + 28 (170's day) = 3 483, and 5 026 + 32 + 45 = 5 103, and each of the 28 Ituri zones is likewise 168 plus the two days' flows. Sitrep 171 continues from that base (Ituri 3 483 + 9 = 3 492; national 5 126) and sitrep 173 too (Ituri 3 532; national 5 198). The footnote under Tableau 2 still says the harmonisation took place, so INSP has not said which base is authoritative. Ituri's zone case counts also return to 168's distribution in 170 (Rwampara 1 267 in 169, 1 203 in 170) but no zone stream is published and the province case totals agree (7 346, 7 380, 7 412), so only deaths are listed.
